name: Social Safety Monitoring Circuit
short_description: Reads facial expressions, vocal prosody, and social familiarity cues to assess social threat and regulate approach-withdraw behavior.

components.name: FACE_VALENCE_READER
components.description: Decodes emotional valence and intent from facial expressions

components.name: PROSODY_ANALYZER
components.description: Extracts emotional tone and intent from vocal characteristics

components.name: FAMILIARITY_DETECTOR
components.description: Assesses degree of social familiarity and trust history

components.name: SOCIAL_THREAT_INTEGRATOR
components.description: Integrates facial, vocal, and familiarity signals to assess social threat

scope_conditions: Visual and auditory access to social agent
key_references: Porges, S. W. (2011). The Polyvagal Theory: Neurophysiological foundations of emotions, attachment, communication, and self-regulation. W.W. Norton.
Adolphs, R. (2002). Neural systems for recognizing emotion. Current Opinion in Neurobiology, 12(2), 169–177.
design_implications: Social environments should facilitate clear nonverbal communication; ensure adequate lighting and acoustic clarity for facial and vocal cue perception
Familiar, repeated social contexts reduce threat perception; design spaces for familiarity-building (e.g., recurring gathering places with consistent members)
